_comment: Provider: Groq, Model: llama-3.3-70b-versatile, Date: 2026-11-18, Finding: sqli-02-nosql.js (javascript.mongodb.nosqli.nosql-injection-req-body)

what_it_is.technical: Unsanitized client input from req.body is passed directly into a MongoDB query operator like db.collection.find(). An attacker can supply a nested query object containing MongoDB operators like $gt or $ne to bypass authentication checks.
what_it_is.simplified: The server accepts an entire object from the user and hands it straight to the database search. An attacker can send special query symbols instead of a normal password to trick the database into matching any user.

why_it_happened.technical: Express body-parser parses JSON payloads into JavaScript objects. Passing req.body.password directly into a MongoDB query allows query-operator injection because MongoDB accepts operator objects in place of literal values.
why_it_happened.simplified: The code trusted whatever the user sent in the request body without checking if it was just a regular string.

how_fix_works.technical: Sanitize query keys using mongo-sanitize or validate that input properties are strictly strings using typeof req.body.password === 'string' before passing them to the database query.
how_fix_works.simplified: Check that the input is an ordinary piece of text and remove any database operators before running the search.

attack_idea: An attacker sends a JSON payload with password set to {"$gt": ""} to authenticate without knowing the actual password.
key_takeaway: Never pass unsanitized request body objects directly into MongoDB find queries; validate data types explicitly.

likely_false_positive.reason: The find query consumes req.body without type assertion or operator sanitization.
